_note: Static, human-edited map from tool name to side-effect class. No model output may change it. Classes: read | reversible_write | irreversible. A tool not listed here is 'unknown' and blocks a task class from being a compile candidate until someone classifies it.

_shell._note: Shell tools are classified by their command, not their name (see shell_effect.py). 'tools' maps a tool name to the argument that holds the command. 'read_commands' lists programs that only read; 'deny' holds argument prefixes that make one write or run something, 'deny_short' single-letter flags that do, 'sub' the allowed subcommands, 'max_args' the most non-flag arguments allowed, 'args_match' a pattern every argument must match in full. A command is 'read' only if every part of it is listed and clean; otherwise it is 'unknown'. This list is a conservative start, to be extended from the commands a fleet actually runs (python -m reflex shell-commands).
